name: Huemul Circuit
region: Los Glaciares National Park and the Southern Ice Field
why: Four days to the edge of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field and down to Lago Viedma's icebergs. The wildest trek you can do from a village.
book: Register at the park visitor centre before you go (compulsory). You need a harness and two carabiners for the river crossings on a rope: rent them in El Chaltén. Part of the route crosses private land with a fee.
water: Glacier streams and lakes; nothing to buy for four days.
dangers: Two tyrolean traverses over glacier rivers on a fixed rope: you must know how to use a harness.
Paso del Viento (about 1,450 m) and Paso Huemul are fully exposed: wait a day if the forecast says over 70 km/h.
Crossing the glacier tongue at Laguna Toro needs care; the route is marked by cairns, not paint.
turnaround: If the wind at Paso del Viento makes you crouch, go back down to Laguna Toro: there is no shelter for 4 hours after it.
